flags.title: Block-Granted Medicaid — Fixed Federal Allocation Regardless of Need
flags.summary: Puerto Rico receives Medicaid through a block grant with a fixed federal allocation — unlike states which receive open-ended matching. This means PR Medicaid is structurally underfunded. When the block grant runs out, the territory must fund 100% of additional costs. Mi Salud: 787-641-2020 / salud.gov.pr.

flags.title: NAP (Block-Granted SNAP) — ~77 Cents Per Dollar of Mainland SNAP
flags.summary: Puerto Rico does NOT receive SNAP. Instead, it receives the Nutrition Assistance Program (NAP), which is block-granted at approximately 77 cents per dollar of what mainland SNAP would provide. NAP benefits are lower and the program has different rules. ADSEF: 787-289-7600 / familia.pr.gov.

flags.title: UI $190/Week — Lowest Unemployment Benefit in Entire Registry
flags.summary: Puerto Rico's unemployment insurance maximum is $190/week — lower than any US state (Mississippi is $235). Duration: up to 26 weeks. PR DOL: 787-754-2119 / trabajo.pr.gov.

flags.title: PROMESA Oversight Board — Federal Austerity Requirements
flags.summary: The Puerto Rico Oversight, Management, and Economic Stability Act (PROMESA) created a federal fiscal oversight board that requires austerity cuts to public services. This affects healthcare, education, and social services funding. Monitor current fiscal plan for service cuts.

flags.title: Hurricane Maria Legacy — Rural Interior Still Recovering
flags.summary: Hurricane Maria (2017) caused catastrophic damage. Rural interior municipalities (Utuado, Jayuya, Adjuntas, Lares) are still recovering with infrastructure gaps. Verify current utility and housing status for rural clients. FEMA: disasterassistance.gov. PR Housing Department: 787-274-2527.

flags.title: US Territory — limited federal program access
Involuntary Hold: Puerto Rico Involuntary Admission
flags.message: PR involuntary psychiatric hold law: Puerto Rico Involuntary Admission. Statutory authority: 24 LPRA § 6153. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in PR retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in PR: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Puerto Rico Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Puerto Rico Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
